newsitem.title: USA: Kansas City Fed's Hoenig sees solid U.S. growth.
newsitem.headline: Kansas City Fed's Hoenig sees solid U.S. growth.

text.p: Thomas Hoenig, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, said Tuesday he expected the U.S. economy to grow steadily at a rate of around 2.0 to 2.5 percent annually.

"As you look at the national economy, after growing rapidly in the second quarter, (it) slowed in the third back toward the two percent growth rate in terms of gross domestic product," Hoenig said in a speech to the Kansas City Chamber of Commerce.
Looking ahead, he said he expected the economy to grow at a rate similar to that of the third quarter.
"We have I think a projection of solid growth going forward of a two to two and a half percent rate for the national economy," Hoenig said.

"We have a healthy economy nationwide," Hoenig said. "We have an economy that grows two to two and a half percent. We can absorb new entrants into the labor force, incomes can increase, and I think we can maintain a lower level of unemployment.

"In terms of monetary policy," he added, "we think the growth rate is two to two and a half percent and that that can be sustained without incurring inflation, and if you get above that, that you threaten inflation."
He said monetary policy cannot increase the long-term growth rate of the economy. although it can be used to bring about price stability. Price stability means neither inflation nor deflation.

An environment of price stability makes it easier to take the actions needed to boost productivity and thus long-term growth, including turning around the recent "disturbing" downward trend in the U.S. savings rate, Hoenig said.
